'''William "Will" Frazer III''' (born 1958) is an American educator.

Frazer worked as a [[Trader (finance)|bond trader]] on [[Financial District, Manhattan|Wall Street]] before becoming a teacher at [[Buchholz High School]] in [[Gainesville, Florida]], where he created and coached the nationally recognized [[List of mathematics competitions#National high school competitions (grade 9–12) and lower|math team]], leading them to 16 of 17 consecutive [[Mu Alpha Theta]] national math championships.<ref name="WSJ">{{cite news |last=Cohen |first=Ben |date=July 14, 2022 |title=How a Public School in Florida Built America's Greatest Math Team |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/the-secrets-of-americas-greatest-high-school-math-team-11657791000 |access-date=March 16, 2025 |work=The Wall Street Journal |archive-date=March 18, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250318175355/https://www.wsj.com/articles/the-secrets-of-americas-greatest-high-school-math-team-11657791000 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2024, Frazer opened The Frazer School, an independent K-12 school in Gainesville that focuses on competitive academics.

== Early life and education ==
Frazer was born and raised in Gainesville, Florida. His father, William Frazer II, was an economics professor at the [[University of Florida]]'s [[Warrington College of Business]].<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |date=July 17, 2016 |title=The Trader Turned Teacher |url=https://news.warrington.ufl.edu/alumni-friends/the-trader-turned-teacher/ |access-date=March 16, 2025 |publisher=University of Florida Warrington College of Business}}</ref> His mother, Mary Ann, was the city clerk of Gainesville and worked as a realtor.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Frazer |first=Will |title=Why his hometown adds up to happiness |url=https://www.gainesville.com/story/lifestyle/magazine/2015/07/31/why-his-hometown-adds-up-to-happiness/31389998007/ |access-date=2025-07-26 |website=Gainesville Sun |language=en-US}}</ref>

Frazer attended Buchholz High School, where he was the first golfer to qualify for the state championship.<ref name=":0" /> He graduated in 1976, then earned a bachelor's degree in accounting from the University of Florida's [[Fisher School of Accounting]] in 1980.<ref name="auto" />

== Finance career ==
In the early 1980s, Frazer worked at [[Lazard|Lazard Frères]] as a bond trader. Years later, he said he hated the [[Financial services|finance-industry]] culture, in which he "just didn't feel healthy".<ref>{{Cite news |last=Carpenter |first=Scott |date=June 3, 2022 |title=Former Trader Turns High School Math Team Into Wall Street Pipeline |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-06-03/ex-trader-turns-high-school-math-team-into-wall-street-pipeline |archive-url=https://archive.today/20220603224208/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-06-03/ex-trader-turns-high-school-math-team-into-wall-street-pipeline |archive-date=June 3, 2022 |access-date=April 9, 2025 |work=Bloomberg |language=en |quote=The money was good, but Frazer’s chain-smoking bosses and the late-night drinking didn’t make a long career on Wall Street seem attractive. "I just didn’t feel healthy," Frazer said.}}</ref>

He retired from the industry at age 27, bought two [[Ferrari]]s, and moved to Black Diamond Ranch, a luxurious [[Country club|golf club]] in [[Lecanto, Florida|Lecanto]], [[Citrus County, Florida|Citrus County]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Strange |first=Deborah |title=Motivation behind the math |url=https://www.gainesville.com/story/news/education/2016/09/24/wall-street-millionaire-trades-it-in-for-gainesville-classroom/25380636007/ |access-date=2025-07-27 |website=Gainesville Sun |language=en-US}}</ref> He moved back to Gainesville a few years later, began coaching golf at [[P. K. Yonge Developmental Research School|P.K. Yonge High School]] and Buchholz High School, and served on the City of Gainesville's pension board.<ref name="auto" />

== Teaching career ==
Frazer started teaching mathematics at Buchholz High School in spring 1997. He initially inquired about teaching a finance course at Buchholz's finance academy, but there were none available, so Buchholz offered Frazer a math course instead.<ref name="auto" /> He founded the Buchholz math team in 1998, and under his leadership, the math team achieved success in state and national competitions. From 2007 to 2016, the team won ten consecutive [[Mu Alpha Theta]] national championships, then six of the next seven.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-07-15 |title=Buchholz wins 16th national math championship |url=https://www.mainstreetdailynews.com/education/buchholz-math-16th-national-win |access-date=2025-07-26 |website=www.mainstreetdailynews.com |language=en-US |archive-date=August 12, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250812174145/https://www.mainstreetdailynews.com/education/buchholz-math-16th-national-win |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023 |title=Championships |url=https://www.buchholzmathteam.com/championships |access-date=March 16, 2025 |publisher=Buchholz Math Team |archive-date=March 18, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250318175351/https://www.buchholzmathteam.com/championships |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Harrell |first=Gershon |date=July 19, 2022 |title=Buchholz High School takes home 14th national math championship win in 15-year span |url=https://www.gainesville.com/story/news/2022/07/19/buchholz-high-school-wins-14th-national-championship/10089688002/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250317032324/https://www.gainesville.com/story/news/2022/07/19/buchholz-high-school-wins-14th-national-championship/10089688002/ |archive-date=March 17, 2025 |access-date=March 17, 2025 |work=Gainesville Sun}}</ref>

In 2022, this success drew national media coverage. ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' described the team as "America's greatest math team" and a “dynasty built by one teacher.”<ref name="WSJ" /> Frazer appeared on ''[[Fox & Friends]]'' to discuss the team's achievements.<ref>{{cite news |date=July 18, 2022 |title=Buchholz Math Team Coach Discusses Success on Fox News |url=https://www.foxnews.com/media/buchholz-math-team-coach-will-frazer-on-winning |access-date=March 16, 2025 |work=Fox News}}</ref> The [[Florida Department of Education]] recognized the Buchholz math program as a model for other schools.<ref name="WSJ" /> Several Florida senators met with Frazer to discuss how the state could reproduce his success.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Carpenter |first1=Scott |date=June 3, 2022 |title=Former Trader Turns High School Math Team Into Wall Street Pipeline |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-06-03/ex-trader-turns-high-school-math-team-into-wall-street-pipeline |archive-url=https://archive.today/20220603224208/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-06-03/ex-trader-turns-high-school-math-team-into-wall-street-pipeline |archive-date=June 3, 2022 |access-date=April 9, 2025 |work=Bloomberg |language=en |quote=Frazer’s achievements have caught the eyes of a group of Florida state senators, who met with him last month to learn how they might replicate Buchholz’s success.}}</ref>

The following year, Frazer said he would leave Buchholz to open an independent academic institution in Gainesville that would focus on competitive academics.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Lawson |first=Lillian |title=A new, private school focusing on competitive academics will open this year |url=https://www.gainesville.com/story/news/education/2024/04/16/private-frazer-school-will-focus-on-academic-competition/73341066007/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250317033121/https://www.gainesville.com/story/news/education/2024/04/16/private-frazer-school-will-focus-on-academic-competition/73341066007/ |archive-date=March 17, 2025 |access-date=March 17, 2025 |work=The Gainesville Sun}}</ref> The Frazer School opened in August 2024.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Voleer |first=Thomas |date=January 28, 2025 |title=Frazer School student among 40 finalists in national science and math competition |url=https://www.yahoo.com/news/frazer-school-student-among-40-144251307.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250317034204/https://www.yahoo.com/news/frazer-school-student-among-40-144251307.html |archive-date=March 17, 2025 |access-date=March 17, 2025 |work=The Gainesville Sun |agency=Yahoo News}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-04-13 |title=New 'Frazer School' to focus on competitive academics |url=https://www.mainstreetdailynews.com/education/will-frazer-buchholz-competitive-academics |access-date=2025-07-26 |website=www.mainstreetdailynews.com |language=en-US |archive-date=May 23, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250523184332/https://www.mainstreetdailynews.com/education/will-frazer-buchholz-competitive-academics |url-status=live }}</ref> It won the 2025 [[Physics Bowl|PhysicsBowl]] World Championship and won the 2025 Mu Alpha Theta national championship. They won the Mu Alpha Theta national championship again in 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Anderson |first=Jon |title=2025 PhysicsBowl Results: Regions 00–14 |url=https://www.aapt.org/Programs/PhysicsBowl/upload/2025-Results-Regions-00_14_updated.pdf |access-date=June 6, 2025 |website=aapt.org |publisher=American Association of Physics Teachers |archive-date=September 20, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250920022342/https://www.aapt.org/Programs/PhysicsBowl/upload/2025-Results-Regions-00_14_updated.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=May 16, 2025 |title=Frazer School physics team wins national AAPT Physics Bowl |url=https://www.mainstreetdailynews.com/education/frazer-school-physics-team-wins-national-aapt-physics-bowl |access-date=June 6, 2025 |archive-date=August 3, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250803014012/https://www.mainstreetdailynews.com/education/frazer-school-physics-team-wins-national-aapt-physics-bowl |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-07-14 |title=Frazer School wins Mu Alpha Theta national championship |url=https://www.mainstreetdailynews.com/education/frazer-school-wins-2025-mu-alpha-theta-national-championship |access-date=2025-07-26 |website=www.mainstreetdailynews.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://famat.org/results/static/reports/Full_Sweepstakes_Indv_Nationals%202026.html |access-date=2026-07-10 |website=famat.org|title=FAMAT Sweepstake results}}</ref>
